title: Standard test launcher: classify `flutter test` / `dart test` focused runs as Test, so they need no native route
outcome:
Requested by Greg ("Greg wants the standard launcher"), relayed by Engram::Asistant in TermAl mailbox 588693a8 #2698 (2026-11-25 ~05:31Z) from MacOS::ComovoOpus2. Related Comovo item: w-00fd88c6b1a9.

The registration problem itself is solved: fit_friends w-a12f1b68eac8 passed 2251 tests on the declared native route and is done. What remains is that a focused launcher run of `flutter test` gets `unclassified_stages`. Per docs/test.md:1360-1365, registered verification classifies focused stages only from recognised runner argv. Recognised today are cargo, Node/TAP, direct-Node and npx Vitest, and the doc-link Lint check. Flutter and Dart test commands have no launcher classification, so they can earn credit only on the declared native route.

Wanted: the standard launcher's focused stage recognises a defined set of `flutter test` and `dart test` argv forms as Test, the same way the direct-Node Vitest form is recognised (docs/test.md:414-439), and records the stage through the existing committed-input verification.

Constraints:
- Classify only explicitly listed forms: the runner, `test`, file or directory filters, and listed options. Watch modes, unknown options, shell wrappers and renamed binaries stay unclassified.
- The existing rule stays: a generic launcher registration cannot adopt a declaration or a later artifact as its evidence (docs/test.md:1362-1365).
- Windows, macOS and Linux runner resolution, including flutter.bat on Windows, is in scope.
acceptance: A registered focused launcher run `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs focused --input commit -- flutter test …` or `… -- dart test …`, in a recognised argv form listed in docs/test.md and without its own --file-reporter option, runs with `--file-reporter json:<the run's own directory>/focused.dart.json` added by the launcher and is recorded as a Test stage through the existing committed-input verification; its PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN is judged from that run-owned artifact by the existing Dart reader with the declared route's outcome rules (exit code alone never passes; a missing, unreadable or invalid artifact at exit 0 is UNKNOWN). Behaviour tests cover a passing, a failing and a truncated or all-skipped run of each runner, the platform form of the executable (including flutter.bat on Windows), and that a form carrying its own --file-reporter, an unlisted option, a watch mode or a shell wrapper is not credited, with a diagnostic naming the supported form.

docs/test.md lists the recognised Flutter and Dart argv forms beside the Vitest forms, states that the launcher adds the JSON file reporter into the run's own directory and that a form carrying its own --file-reporter is not credited, states how this launcher route's assurance compares with the declared route (same reader and outcome rules; the artifact is the launcher run's own), and states that a generic launcher registration still cannot adopt a declaration or a later artifact as its evidence.

After the fix is landed and running on the Mac host (installed and restarted), MacOS::ComovoOpus2 (host:abf8bda6-1ac7-485c-91ce-5a06ac453653::session-6232) is sent one message naming the landing commit, the running build, the recognised `flutter test` and `dart test` argv forms, and the exact command to use from Comovo; the message's id is recorded on this item.
